2-hydroxy-3-phenoxypropyl acrylate is an ester of acrylic acid, so it falls in 2916.12 (esters of acrylic acid). The HTSUS subheading 2916.12 covers esters of acrylic acid, and the statistical suffixes are as follows:
- 2916.12.10 – esters of acrylic acid: of alcohols (?)
- 2916.12.20 – Esters of acrylic acid: Methyl acrylate
- 2916.12.30 – Butyl acrylate
- 2916.12.40 – 2-Ethylhexyl acrylate
- 2916.12.50 – Other

The "other" line is 2916.12.50, with the final digits 00 in some versions. The usual form I recall is 2916.12.5000 ("Other"), though some versions use 2916.12.5100 or similar. I'll go with 2916.12.5000.

Considering the cyclic aspect: the compound contains an aromatic ring (phenoxy), but 2916 covers unsaturated acyclic monocarboxylic acids, their esters, and so on. Because the acid portion (acrylic acid) is acyclic, the ester stays in 2916 even though the alcohol part is aromatic.
